title: Elodie and the Well
premise: Astrid Sterling, a new teacher at Hollowmere Primary, inherits his grandmother's house and discovers that every old photograph now contains an extra chair — the chair of a boy who vanished from the school in 1974, the year Astrid's grandmother served as caretaker of the well on its grounds. The missing-class problem is no accident: something beneath the well takes a child each harvest moon, sustained by a bargain the grandmother made to save her own son. Astrid must uncover what was taken in 1974 — a name, a memory, and a life — and return it to the well before the harvest moon rises, even if returning it means surrendering the identity he has spent five years constructing. In the end, Astrid gives back what was taken, freeing the lost children but erasing himself from every photograph in the house except one: an empty chair, waiting.
about_author: Oscar Kavanagh is a former rural schoolteacher who spent a decade collecting local legends about wells, harvests, and disappearances across the English countryside. He writes horror rooted in domestic inheritance, insisting that the scariest houses are the ones we're given rather than the ones we choose.

chapters.title: The Extra Chair
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Moving into his late grandmother's house, he sorts through decades of family photographs and notices the same impossible detail: an empty wooden chair appears in pictures taken years apart, always at the edge of frame. He tells himself it's a printing artifact. The beat is quiet unease — the rational mind bending around evidence it can't dismiss.

chapters.title: Hollowmere Primary
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. His first week teaching Year 6 at a school with a strange reputation: three children have gone 'missing' over fifty years, each around the autumn equinox. Colleagues deflect; the headmistress, Mrs. Vane, watches him too closely. Beat: professional optimism shadowed by institutional secrecy.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A student, Imogen Pryce, asks him why the school register has pages torn out for October 1974. That night, checking the house's records, he finds his grandmother was the school caretaker until 1975 — then abruptly resigned. Beat: the first thread connecting house to school.

chapters.title: What the Photographs Want
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The extra chair begins moving closer to the center of each photograph as he studies them, night by night. In one 1974 image, a boy sits in it — face blurred beyond recognition. Astrid starts sleeping with the lights on. Beat: dread escalating into obsession.

chapters.title: The Well on School Grounds
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. He explores the sealed well behind the old boiler room, capped with concrete and chained, though the chain is bright and new. Imogen follows him there and says her dead great-uncle 'lives down there.' Beat: childlike certainty colliding with adult denial.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. In the attic he finds a ledger in his grandmother's hand, recording dates, names, and payments — entries ending in 1974 with a single line: 'It is paid. It will not ask again.' The final page lists a boy's name, half-burned. Beat: grief curdling into suspicion of someone he loved.

chapters.title: Mrs. Vane Knows
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Astrid and Mrs. Vane. She confronts him gently, revealing she was a pupil in 1974 and remembers the day Tommy Ellery vanished — and remembers Astrid's grandmother carrying a wrapped bundle from the well at dawn. Beat: two keepers of a secret circling each other.

chapters.title: Five Years of Noises
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, flashback-heavy. We learn why Astrid has spent five years explaining away noises: since a breakdown he refuses to name, he has trained himself to rationalize everything. The house's sounds — dragging, knocking, a child humming — test that discipline to breaking. Beat: vulnerability exposed; identity as armor.

chapters.title: Imogen Draws the Chair
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Imogen turns in homework: a drawing of a wooden chair with a boy sitting in it, labeled 'Tommy.' She says Tommy told her Astrid would come. Astrid reports it to Mrs. Vane, who goes white and orders him off the case. Beat: the past reaching into the present through a child.

chapters.title: The Harvest Moon Calendar
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Cross-referencing the ledger with lunar tables, Astrid realizes every disappearance fell on a harvest moon — and this year's falls in eleven days. The concrete cap on the well has begun to sweat warm water. Beat: a countdown begins; helplessness becomes urgency.

chapters.title: Return What Was Taken
chapters.summary: Mrs. Vane's POV. She confesses the family bargain: the thing in the well grants long life or saved loved ones in exchange for a child every generation, and the Sterlings have been its wardens. To end it, whatever was taken in 1974 must be returned willingly. Beat: exposition as burden; complicity across generations.

chapters.title: Tommy Ellery, Age Nine
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Researching archives, Astrid learns Tommy wasn't abducted — he drowned in the well during a game, and Astrid's grandmother, panicking over her own son's safety, offered the entity a trade: Tommy's body and name in exchange for her boy's life. Beat: the horror of love weaponized; inheritance as guilt.

chapters.title: Her Boy
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, devastating midpoint turn. Astrid finds his own birth record altered and realizes the 'boy' saved in 1974 was him — that he died, briefly, and was remade, which is why he has spent five years explaining away noises, memories, and a self that never quite fit. Beat: identity collapses; the theme lands personally.

chapters.title: The Chair Sits Empty
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Every photograph in the house now shows the chair front and center, facing the viewer, and Astrid's own image is fading at the edges. The humming upstairs has stopped — replaced by patience. Beat: the calm before the climax; being erased while still alive.

chapters.title: Imogen Is Chosen
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Imogen stops coming to class. Her parents say she's 'staying with relatives'; her desk holds a drawing of the well with a small figure descending. The cycle intends to continue unless the debt is settled first. Beat: stakes become immediate and moral — a teacher cannot abandon a pupil.

chapters.title: Down the Boiler Room Stairs
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. On the night before the harvest moon, Astrid breaks the chain and pries the cap. The well breathes out warm air smelling of cut hay and pond water. Something below says his childhood nickname, one only his grandmother knew. Beat: threshold crossed; terror laced with terrible familiarity.

chapters.title: The Ones Who Waited
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, dreamlike descent. At the bottom he finds not a monster but a crowded dark: generations of taken children, including Tommy, preserved and waiting, kept 'safe' the way his grandmother once kept him safe. They do not blame him. They want to go home. Beat: horror transfigured into compassion.

chapters.title: The Bargain Refused
chapters.summary: Mrs. Vane's POV. Vane arrives at the well intending to offer herself in Astrid's place, repeating her predecessors' logic — power used to protect, corruption dressed as sacrifice. Astrid, from below, refuses the trade outright. Beat: the cycle's logic confronted and broken.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. As the moon crests, Astrid speaks the return: Tommy's name restored to the world, his own borrowed life offered back. The well accepts — but because Astrid returns it freely rather than losing it, the entity's claim ends. The children rise like bubbles of light. Beat: climax; surrender transformed into agency.

chapters.title: Morning Register
chapters.summary: Mrs. Vane's POV. Dawn: Imogen walks out of the fog onto school grounds, remembering nothing but feeling 'returned.' The register's torn pages are whole again. Tommy Ellery's name appears in the 1974 records as having moved away. Vane weeps over paperwork. Beat: relief braided with erasure.

chapters.title: The House Without Him
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, penultimate. Astrid wakes in his grandmother's house diminished — half-remembered, translucent in mirrors, absent from every photograph but present enough to teach one last term. He gives the house to Imogen's family and packs a single bag. Beat: bittersweet acceptance; identity rebuilt from choice rather than history.

chapters.title: One Chair, Waiting
chapters.summary: Final chapter, shifting between Astrid's voice and an epilogue narration. Years later, a new teacher finds one photograph in the house's attic: a boy in a wooden chair, smiling faintly, captioned in Astrid's handwriting — 'Returned.' Somewhere, Astrid finally hears silence, and calls it home. Beat: resolution; inheritance redeemed as memory freely given.
